name: Urolithiasis, Acute Renal Colic, and Endourological Procedures

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Campbell-Walsh Urology 12th ed
clinicalPearls: Non-contrast helical CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis is the diagnostic gold standard for urolithiasis
Obstructing stone accompanied by fever, hydronephrosis, or urosepsis requires emergency decompression
Distal ureteral stones smaller than 5 mm pass spontaneously in 75% under alpha-blocker expulsive therapy
Struvite stones form in alkaline urine secondary to urease-producing bacteria (Proteus mirabilis)
Staghorn calculi and renal stones exceeding 20 mm are managed with percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL)
reference.pathophysiology: Urolithiasis results from supersaturation of urine with lithogenic solute ions exceeding crystallization inhibitory thresholds. Calcium oxalate precipitation produces the vast majority of stones. Proteus infections produce urease, hydrolyzing urea to ammonia and carbon dioxide, elevating urine pH and driving magnesium ammonium phosphate struvite deposition into branching pelvicalyceal staghorn calculi.
additionalDifferentials: Ruptured or leaking abdominal aortic aneurysm
Renal cell carcinoma with hematuria and clot colic
additionalInvestigations: Non-contrast helical CT of kidneys, ureters, and bladder (NCCT KUB)
Urinalysis, urine microscopy for crystals, and urine culture
Serum creatinine, electrolytes, calcium, and uric acid
24-hour urine metabolic evaluation (calcium, oxalate, citrate, uric acid)
